title: Quantum Mott semimetal in a one-dimensional Hubbard mode
authors: Boran Zhou, Taige Wang, Ya-Hui Zhang
abstract: Mott physics in topological bands has recently attracted considerable attention, particularly in the context of twisted bilayer graphene (TBG). However, the essential ingredients for stabilizing this physics remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate a quantum Mott semimetal phase as the ground state within a one-dimensional spinful Hubbard model featuring only one orbital per unit cell, protected by inversion and particle-hole symmetries. We start from a two-orbital model where a localized $f$ orbital on the A sublattice hybridizes with a delocalized $c$ orbital on the B sublattice. Projecting the $f$-orbital Hubbard $U$ onto the active flat band yields a lattice model with Wannier orbitals centered on the B sublattice. Similar to TBG, a momentum-space scale $k_*$ emerges, setting the interaction range in the projected model to $1/k_*$. While the ground state is ferromagnetic with only the Hubbard $U$, introducing an inter-site antiferromagnetic spin coupling $J$ stabilizes a Mott semimetal$^*$ phase with a central charge $c=3$. Using exact diagonalization (ED) and density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) methods, we show that this phase hosts a spinful Dirac fermion coexisting with a neutral spin mode -- analogous to the fractionalized Fermi liquid (FL$^*$) phase in higher dimensions. Furthermore, breaking particle-hole (PH) symmetry via dispersion transforms the Mott semimetal into a Mott insulator, which is separated from a distinct Mott insulating phase by a continuous transition with a polarization jump of $1/2$. Our work provides the first unbiased evidence of a Mott semimetal ground state and demonstrates that this 1D model captures some essential aspects of TBG physics, despite lacking a Wannier obstruction.
summary: This work theoretically establishes a novel Quantum Mott semimetal phase in a 1D Hubbard model, providing evidence for its existence and characterizing its low-energy excitations. By combining DMRG, RG theory, and spectral analysis, the authors map out how this state transitions between different insulating phases based on symmetry breaking. It offers a crucial theoretical framework for understanding correlated physics analogous to that found in materials like twisted bilayer graphene.
main_problem: The study aims to demonstrate a quantum Mott semimetal phase and understand its connection to physics observed in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG). It also characterizes the low-energy effective theory of this state.
main_result: The authors provide evidence for a stable Mott semimetal ground state stabilized by an antiferromagnetic coupling, which hosts a spinful Dirac fermion coexisting with a neutral spin mode. They also map out transitions between different Mott insulating phases based on symmetry breaking.
method: The research employs advanced theoretical techniques including Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG), Exact Diagonalization (ED), Bosonization, and Renormalization Group (RG) analysis to analyze the system's ground state properties.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional spinful Hubbard model derived from projecting an $f$-orbital Hubbard interaction onto an active flat band. It incorporates hopping ($t$), on-site interactions ($U$), and inter-site exchange couplings ($J$).
key_observables: Central charge (c), spin correlator decay ($\sim r^{-1}$), spectral functions $A(k, \omega)$, and many-body polarization ($P$).
important_parameters: The momentum scale $k^*$, the Hubbard interaction $U$, and the inter-site coupling $J$ are crucial parameters controlling the phase transitions.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include projecting the system onto a flat band, using approximations like the Hubbard-I approximation for spectral calculations, and assuming stability within numerical precision limits for DMRG/RG analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic models (two-orbital setup), phase diagrams showing transitions between different Mott phases ($P=1/2$ vs $P=0$), and quantitative results like entanglement entropy confirming central charge values.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the model from a two-orbital system, then using DMRG/ED to identify the semimetal phase characterized by $c=3$. Subsequent analysis uses low-energy effective theories (Bosonization/RG) and spectral function calculations to map out stability boundaries and understand the nature of the gapless excitations.
why_interesting: The detailed theoretical mapping using RG flow equations to determine the stability of exotic quantum phases like Mott semimetals is highly relevant for understanding strongly correlated materials where simple mean-field approaches fail.
